Two vocabularies, one classifier

Why the visual-style gate rejected the visual style · 2026-07-26

The rule defines two separate lists

src/rules/visual-style.md

  ## The Twelve-Glyph Vocabulary     governs EMOJI
     white-check, red-X, warning, refresh, pause, light-bulb,
     siren, target, fire, scroll, robot, lightning, circles, medals

  ## ASCII Palette                   governs DIAGRAMS
     Box drawing:  ┌─┐ │ ┘─└   ╔═╗ ║ ╝═╚
     Dividers:     ───  ═══
     Arrows:       → ↓ ▶ ◀
     Progress:     ▓▓▓░░  ████████░░
     Bullets:      • ◦ ‣

find_violations checked only the first list. Every character in the second was therefore reported as “emoji outside the 12-glyph vocabulary” — in a repo whose own rule says “ASCII boxes, tables, diagrams — all encouraged”.

Why the classifier cannot tell them apart

def is_emoji(ch):
    return unicodedata.category(ch) == "So" or ord(ch) >= 0x1F000
characterglyphcategoryclassified
U+2500 box drawing─ └ ├ │ ┌Soemoji
U+2588 blocks█ ▓ ░Soemoji
U+25B6 arrows▶ ◀Soemoji
U+2705 white-check✅Sorescued by VOCAB
U+00B7 middot·Posurvives
U+2190 arrow←Smsurvives

Box drawing and emoji share Unicode category So (Symbol-other). Without an explicit table the classifier genuinely cannot separate them — so the fix is a table, not a looser regex.

The fix, scoped deliberately

ASCII_PALETTE_RANGES
   U+2500 – U+257F   Box Drawing      ┌ ─ ┐ │ └ ┘ ├ ┤ ╔ ═ ╗ ║ ╭ ╮ ╰ ╯
   U+2580 – U+259F   Block Elements   █ ▓ ▒ ░  + eighth-block bar meters

ASCII_PALETTE_CHARS   ▶  ◀  ◦        (palette's arrows + bullets rows)

EXCLUDED on purpose
   U+2700 – U+27BF   Dingbats         ✓ ✗ live here — the rule redirects
                                      these to the white-check / red-X

Body mode

  • palette allowed
  • emoji vocabulary only
  • dingbats still rejected

Title mode — unchanged

  • palette still rejected
  • emoji still rejected
  • rule: titles stay plain ASCII

The doc had no PR-body entry at all. That silence is how the validator ended up inventing a policy stricter than any documented surface. This PR adds the entry, so the next reader finds the rule where the rule lives instead of inferring it from a CI failure.
